This past weekend we visited the old school movie theater and there were two shows playing simultaneously that night: "The Sandlot" and "Explorer 9." One of them happened to be showing "Caddyshack." We had never seen either film before so we knew nothing about them (except the fact that they're both comedies), but decided to go check it out anyway. Well.. it turns out that they were both great movies. Although Caddy Shack might've been better off just having one film played, the other was definitely more entertaining than the first one. Great fun!! Both were directed by Mel Brooks, perhaps best known as director of Blazing Saddles and Fletch, although he has also written over 300 films. Unlike some people who know little about comedy when they see a comedian's show or read their book (not me!), Mel Brooks actually knows what he's talking about when it comes to comedy. His ability to keep things light-hearted while still making jokes that can really stick around is probably the reason why his movies become almost as popular today as they did back then. Of course, you'll find no shortage of hysterical antics in his films, ranging from slapstick humor (the movie's title) through jokes involving cars, food, women, etc. Although some movies give you the impression that the cast members work together well because they're friends, most of the time it seems that everyone gets along very well - or even better, that everyone hates each other (it's rare). But the truth is, most comedians aren't as good as Mel Brooks at creating funny characters. They can make you laugh until your sides hurt, but that doesn't mean they get away with being bad actors. Maybe the best example of this is the character Steve Martin's character in Coming To America. When he was growing up, his dad didn't treat him right; however, after coming home to the U.S. every day, the father treated Steve exactly how he used to act toward his children - which was awesome. Some people don't seem to understand how much talent a comic needs to create an effective standup routine. However, since he creates comebacks, characters, plotlines and entire seasons, you'd think Steve Martin wouldn't need any help. Unfortunately, many people look for what it takes to be successful instead of developing skills to succeed. That's why they don't find success. Furthermore, many comics will tell themselves, "he isn't that good," or "I'm too old." Their failure to realize the larger point behind everything they do makes them look foolish rather than smart. But I believe that does make some sense... Why should an intelligent person change their behavior solely based on what others think? If someone thinks you're dumb enough to watch those crappy Disney cartoons everybody else watches, maybe they shouldn't be giving you free advice. Plus, with what's going on nowadays, nearly anyone could put on a pair of prosthetic arms and start saying whatever they want without worrying about whether or not their words sway a few hearts.

BEING SORT OF A NARCISSIST, I STARTED WRITING A MEMOIR... CHAPTER 3: WHAT I LEARNED IN JUNIOR HIGH Inspired after reading about Pablo Picasso's legendary ways with women, I drew on that for my junior high middle school drama class. I wrote a bunch of jokes and one guy in our group was so into it he laughed out loud every time the teacher read lines like, "He never noticed her face or the way his clothing fell off." Finally, she lifted her hand to show him where they'd got stuck and he just sneered at her as if nothing had happened. So when we were done writing this scene - which ended up being about a girl who wanted to impress her boyfriend - I felt bad because I understood why the boy didn't share his laughter with anyone else. But then I thought how much better if he did! As the story progressed, I learned that it wasn't about me, but rather what happens when people don't share their feelings or laugh at other people's jokes. At first, I struggled with the idea of my character hanging herself, but I decided to let loose since it would be more true to reality than if I hadn't. When a few boys found out (and there are so many episodes), I cried. Oh and yes, the rest of the story is based largely on real events, although some parts are exaggerated or changed slightly.

Coming back home, we stayed overnight at the hotel which we loved. At least there isn't traffic waiting to make your trip easier because there always seems to be plenty of parking spots open between the hotel rooms! It hasn't been easy getting used to living apart from our family here because it feels like there weren't really many guests left in our community yet. We've already done some traveling with our family trips, however, making land miles that stretch farther away than typical our family travels usually do allowing us to spend more time together doing things close by such as shopping. We haven't seen our family members recently although we plan to visit soon afterward once the restrictions expire scheduled visits are lifted again. If you're planning your next vacation to visit one of these locations please let us know how you liked our experience at Whittier Hotel!

The couple used to live together but lived separately from Mason when Mason married Mason's mother, and Maggie says she felt a little guilty about leaving Mason alone throughout their marriage because Mason had just gotten engaged this past year and Maggie wasn't expecting them to be living apart anymore until Mason got married last summer. Maggie says she realized Mason could feel betrayed by his former girlfriend without Mason being there during times when he didn't visit. Maggie says Mason passed away suddenly while living together last June; Maggie says Mason never contacted her about it either. Maggie adds that Mason always told her about her ex-boyfriend's death. "I knew Mason would want us to leave him behind," Maggie said. "We were devastated as well - we hadn't seen him since we both graduated school back in 2015. I thought we should stay in our home town, get over everything, move our families around, marry each other. But Mason kept telling us all along that he loved us dearly enough already. We've done most things together since then except date girls. Mason seemed to know exactly what we needed to do!" Maggie added. "And Mason has taught Maggie that staying longer doesn't mean you'll miss your significant others. Now she sees life differently." While Maggie misses Mason regularly watching her boyfriend play basketball games or working outside with his friends, Maggie admits that the longer she spends seeing Mason fewer days are spent together. "When Mason goes away the conversations Stop cause we can fight more than we normally would due to our busy schedules," she explained. "Truly, we don't talk enough to see each other often. Maggie also observes Mason rarely visits Mason's apartment, preferring to spend time outdoors instead. Every year I get excited about the opportunity to step into "the culture" and try something new - especially if it's something I haven't tried before or not yet experienced abroad; a new language, restaurant, hotel, or night club. We had a blast exploring Finland without food restrictions because we could roll up our sleeves and eat whatever choice of beer we'd like (and drink whatever beverages we wanted!) The difference between our experiences is obvious: We enjoyed the whole experience together but it wasn't just traveling alone! The culture split apart over time well beyond our desiresWithin the first month, we were hooked by the amazing Finnish cuisine, architecture, and cultural heritage. The feeling of familiarity didn't feel overwhelming until we arrived at the hotel town of Fenno which meant leaving our hotel room early one morning to buy some breakfast cereal for breakfast right outside our door. When we sat down and ate we talked about the book "Eggs," a book full of fascinating facts about Finland's history and geography brought us back again and again. Start your day off right by grabbing a beer and dodging the crowds visiting the nearby ski resorts of Falle. You'll find plenty of cute little restaurants serving tasty hot dogs perched atop pine trees near the slopes overlooking the mountains where you can enjoy meals such as hamachi noodles topped with fresh scallops and salmon served sans lobster sauce. Finnish cuisine has its roots in the national folklore, so visit Helsinki to learn about its traditions and celebrate Finland's national dishes including Akatekua and Rotelhoppa starfish cakes featuring different kind of fish balls with a salt pepper sauce made entirely using soy sauce. The Finnish restaurants offer authentic food offerings like soup pot soups followed by ice cream sundae options including Grilled Fish Soup and Ojoko Fajita. When you arrive you'll discover many more places where you can sample delicious dishes prepared exactly what you want and stay overnight. You may also explore Helsinki's colorful area where restaurants provide delicious dining choices ranging from Finnish cuisine to seafood dishes. After spending five days laying low enjoying our Finnish winter nights away from the hustling city life, we returned home refreshed and ready to take a trip around Finland! Now we spend time exploring various destinations throughout Finland trying to make sense of the world behind closed doors:) SOURCE Helsinki International Convention Centre

There's plenty of seating areas inside too. It's always hard to know where to start after finishing a book such as A River So Wide: An American Summer by Sylvia Plath. This memoir chronicles the life of one of America's most famous poets during her formative teenage years- from childhood through high school, college days, early writerly experiences including her successes along with struggles ranging from depression to alcoholism to attempted suicide-and ultimately her death just weeks before she turned 25. In fact, Sylvia helped create the word "poem" itself, writing "The Sculpture Garden" shortly after graduation from Smith College and publishing it under her own name only two months later. And yet, despite growing fame, readers learn about Sylvia's troubled relationship with her mother, a woman who left much to be desired; excessive drinking and drug abuse led to many visits to the hospital; and her student status meant frequent unsupervised travel abroad with her friend Maynard Keynes, leading them both into dangerous situations. Fortunately, while struggling artists often suffer the consequences of their choices and struggle alone, Sylvia found support within herself - including spiritual guidance - and maintained stability throughout the course of her career. And although it's impossible to come away with empathy for all of her characters, especially those nearing the end of their lives, reading A River So Wide allows us to understand certain aspects of Sylvia's journey and experience. For example, students studying modern literature could gain understanding of some contemporary issues facing young adults today-such as anxiety over social media usage, insecurity around body image, gender identity concerns, and various mental health challenges. Furthermore, scholars studying poetry might find inspiration from Sylvia's work and its significance-writing poems inspired by difficult circumstances, like transience in "A Tree Shall Rise Again." Finally, recent history buffs would likely recognize several literary symbols and iconic locations featured in the tale, particularly the presence of the English Lake District and Switzerland. (Students learning Spanish may want to look carefully for references to local landmarks.) A deep appreciation of language and poetics contribute significantly to the novel's beauty. As mentioned previously, Sylvia writes beautiful lines from beginning to end, creating vivid imagery and using metaphor effectively. That said, because of the theme of loss, easily accessible words have little meaning unless they are paired properly with powerful images. Consequently, students should pay attention to precise diction used throughout the text. Their focus must include structure, rhythm, tone, sound effects, repetition, imagery, simile, and phraseology-in addition to vocabulary appropriate to age level, genre, context and purpose.

Don't be tempted by the cheap rates, this is the worst hotel, EVER. I booked my trip through Orbitz for two nights including car rental. After flying in from New York, we decided to try out a new restaurant on our first night there and had planned on returning to our hotel room at 10:00 pm (arrive at 8:30 am). There was no phone number anywhere either....so now here we are trying to figure out how to call someone to let us in...we're going nuts while standing outside in the 100 degree heat not knowing if anyone knows anything about getting access inside this place. They both tell us that we aren't allowed visitors during regular business hours..even though the policy doesn't say we can't have guests? The lady finally gives up and goes back to work leaving us stuck outside wondering what do with ourselves??? A young man then approaches us telling us that the fire department will probably break down the door ASAP since it expires within 30 min's of being closed??? WHAT???? He also mentions that there isn't any food in the fridge and he offered to bring McDonalds over to us?! Are you kidding me??? Well needless to say, we never got inside this horrible hotel and instead went straight from the airport directly to California Pizza Kitchen located a few blocks away......LOL!!!!!!!!!

This place is located in Aria across from Marquee. I was told this was one of the top burger spots on the strip and they weren't lying. I would not have ordered it without hearing about it first but once I did, I could see why people rave so much. The space looks very industrial with a lot going for it including an amazing bar area that you can order drinks at or just hang out while your food arrives since there are plenty of booths to sit around. The menu also comes up as your phone when ordering which is pretty neat feature that helps cut down on wait time if you want something particular (which I highly recommend). As far as burgers go though nothing super fancy like Rive Gauche or In-N-Out but what makes their burger stand apart is how fresh each ingredient is. For example my croissant bun had melded together perfectly and didn't look factory made. Their meat patties were extremely juicy despite being fairly thin and their cheese blend worked really well too. They offer different sides such as fries, onion rings and tater tots along with chili mac and potato salad if you're looking to try more than just the burger (though the main attraction isn't bad either!) If you love Five Guys then this place will give them another run for their money because these guys offer some great choices for both vegetarians and those who don't eat red meat. It's quite expensive though! Dining alone here costs 16-18 per person depending on whether you choose alcohol. Be ready to shell out over 30 dollars before tax and tip. That said, if you take advantage of drink specials during happy hour prices drop back down significantly. Overall, this is definitely worth checking out even if you don't normally care for burger joints!

It did have some interesting exhibitions outside like gardens for example: Garden Room and Horticultural Hall where Queen Elizabeth 2 spent time planting her roses and other flowers herself after she married Prince Andrew in 1773 there, plus also the Royal Mews which displayed some mares including one belonging to Anne Hathaway who had recently got engaged, thus making history today by being the first royal bride to ride over Westminster Bridge unaccompanied. Moments later we arrived at Shilthorpe Manor House just north of Luton near Bedfordshire; an 18th century manor house set amongst acres upon acres of beautiful sprawling grounds. This place was absolutely stunning. From the moment we stepped foot into the main entrance hall we couldn't help but be completely mesmerised by the grandeur of it all as well as feeling somewhat overwhelmed. Everything about the building oozed elegance and class even down to little details such as the ornate mirrors covering almost every inch of wall space throughout the entire estate. Most rooms containing paintings or statues from ancient times further added to the beauty of the place while the way everything was decorated gave everyone the impression that this was once home to royalty. Being located just south of Leicester Square the location itself is perfect for anyone interested in performing arts considering it sits just round the corner from the famous Savoy Theatre meaning a host of stars would often come here for performances. At night they hold regular open air concerts featuring operatic singers, ballet dancers etc. However, with winter approaching fast the theatre company decided to postpone their latest production for next year. I highly recommend Ristorante Orlando even though it's outside my normal eating style because the food and wines are truly top quality beyond comparison. In fact, I hope they open up other locations throughout Kansas City so they can become more accessible to those who love Italian cuisine!

AOA,The only thing keeping the lid on the washer door is gravity once it finally gets loose enough to fall completely off-it then goes into the outer tub which has holes in both sides for draining. It sometimes happens when you do big loads and things pile up between where the front edge of the top of the inner tub sits against the bottom edge of the outside tub-the weight of whatever is piled up pushes down slightly more than you think until eventually the top starts floating away slowly but noticeably until it falls off causing leaks inside. If the water level lowers to far after it stops leaking on its own though it ends up taking awhile to dry out as it takes time for the air pockets created by the leak to evaporate as well as sucking moisture up through those drain holes. On many washers anyway-others may still drip even without the lid staying on too tightly. You mentioned you had water in your basement..that happened recently while using mine also. Like others experienced, after doing laundry and letting the clothes hang to dry everything stopped working properly. Everything else just slowed way down and worked normally including drying. About 3 hours later I heard the sound of rushing waters, I looked around and saw water coming in my garage. Now instead of filling the machine it filled my subfloor area and ended up flooding nearly half of my basement. After cleaning everything up and crying myself to sleep that night, I decided to research online and found lots of posts like yours describing your exact experience! That's exactly how mine went down except it didn't stop running and make noises first, just started being slow. Once the flood came and ruined my carpet and electronics I got pissed enough to want to find something better. I ended up replacing it today and bought a Maytag Mz2522LW top loader front load washer. Now that I have seen your post I hope I don't run into anything similar! Thanks everyone for sharing.

The restaurant has a gorgeous interior design by Robert Auerbach of New York City's Metropolitan Museum of Art. It has panoramic views of Rock Creek Park along with wonderful service. However, these are not reasons why one would spend 200 on a meal there. The reason is the quality of the ingredients used. Even a simple baked potato is made with tender Yukon Gold potatoes imported from Canada instead of the par-cooking mashed reds or russets Americans typically expect. This makes the heftier flavors stand out more because their textures are so much different than those of traditional methods. In addition to excellence in preparation though, there was also excellent wine pairings. But most importantly, there really exists no better steakhouse anywhere. And even if there did exist such a superior establishment, I don't think anyone could justify spending almost double as much money just to duplicate its experience. This was the first time i'd ever been to Ruth Chris Steak House, and oh boy was i blown away!! 1st let me mention how absolutely stunning the building looks inside..like truly beautiful art work..with the woodwork done beautifully throughout each room. Then the whole staff is very friendly, professional, courteous, etc. then comes the BEST part...THE FOOD!!! All around amazing..from the salads, soups, sides, creamed corn, bread pudding, desserts, martinis, coffee, tea, etc. Everything tasted incredible! The only thing we didn't care for was the price tag...at least 200 per person without any drinks or tip added on!!!! Ouch, but totally worth it!!! If your looking for the best of the best when dining out, look no further than here!!

I love this place. After seeing the hotel on Top Chef, I couldn't wait to step foot into this landmark (in my mind, at least). It looked a lot smaller than what it is in real life, but those two things were of little concern because we spent most of our time inside their restaurant and outside with their food truck! We went for dinner on Sunday night while visiting NYC - so that's not too late...but also not super early either. Our waiter was very friendly, informed us about the menu items specials, helped me choose wine pairings for the house cocktails AND he brought out complementary breads before each course arrived! And when trying something new? Get paired up w someone who knows just how to work your palate; A la carte options are extremely reasonably priced as well (20-30 per person)!! We even ordered dessert after finishing dinner! They have an amazing selection of cheeses from all over Europe including some hard to find ones like Comte d'Affinois or Parmigiano Reggiano if you're really interested! Our favorites included: The Roasted Chicken Salad (wonderful greens dressing), Poutine Fries Blue Cheese Sauce (the best poutine fries anywhere!), Fried Green Tomatoes Bacon Cornbread Dressing (so yummy!) along with Pork Belly Tacos stuffed w local farm pork pickled red onions which surprisingly had fresh jalapenos added to them instead of being dryly sauteed. My BF loved his small pizza; I liked mine better. There are lots of gluten free options here too! Overall, can't say enough good things about this restaurant experience... especially considering it wasn't during peak hours! Highly recommend checking this one off your list if you haven't already!

First of all BIG shoutout to Joseph. He is my man. I love their food. You can't go wrong with a number one combo, or a GCC, or both. Great evening out with adults or parties. We love going with our kids the food is great! The staff are always friendly and helpful. BEING SORT OF A NARCISSIST, I STARTED WRITING A MEMOIR... CHAPTER 3: WHAT I LEARNED IN JUNIOR HIGH Inspired after reading about Pablo Picasso's legendary ways with women, I drew the conclusion that if he could do it and get away with it, surely anyone who knew how to handle a pencil and write or draw well should be able to have some fun! I didn't know whether this had any basis in reality but was determined to discover for myself. My friends were more than willing to go along; we began plotting our initial strategy before leaving school one day. We decided to spread out over the lunch period so as not to raise suspicion and sit at different tables within sight of each other but far enough apart to avoid being overheard by teachers when they called around. As luck would have it, my favorite teacher sat next to me. He seemed like quite an ordinary guy and none of us thought there'd be much danger from him so long as we kept things on a low key level. The plan went smoothly without incident until right near the end of lunch time when we heard Mr. Hall call my name. This meant only one thing - everyone scattered except moi (as usual). Mr. Hall stood behind his desk and leaned towards me as though talking into my ear. "Mark?" "Yes sir," I answered, trying desperately to keep cool while practically choking down what felt like a large lump on my tongue. "Did you bring your homework today Mark?" "Oh yeah," I said, relieved that perhaps this whole ordeal wasn't going to come back to haunt me later. Maybe he just wanted to make sure I came prepared for class tomorrow? His voice sounded worried now. Was something wrong? Had I missed something? No matter what it was, I couldn't let anything slip up or I'd never hear the end of it from my parents. At last Mr. Hall cleared his throat, still leaning eerily close to my facePosted by

Never mix Johnnie Walker with Panda Express NO BUENO. I ordered the fried rice and orange flavor chicken followed up with a brisk rasberry ice tea. Normally I would enjoy this pairing, but not today! In my experience Johnnie Walker has always been very smooth and light in taste which is why it's recommended for beginners or those who aren't fans of whiskey because there isn't much to cover up any unpleasant flavors that may be present like many bourbons do... But today im tasting some robust notes mixed into an otherwise smooth drinking scotch; the aged dry smokey peaty malts combined with the fruity sweet sherry cask finish make me think "huh? This drink didn't add anything new to the already established flavors in this fine dram so i couldn't help but feel this drink was just thrown together hastily as a gimmick in order to attract more customers at lunch time. The food itself however was good (although not great) So overall i give panda express 3 stars: Good

please dont go!!! Most likely the puppies there are under weight. I purchased a black German Shepard puppy for 900. She was on sale, beacuse she was to big for her age. That should have been a red flag! When I got her, she was so skinny and weak. She had to be put on a feeding schedule and gained weight slowly. It took about a month for her to reach a healthy weight. She is now 6 months old and doing very well, but she will be small for the rest of her life. The breeder told me that they kept the dogs in kennels with concrete floors while they are breeding them, so they can see what the pups are made of. This is NOT true!! They keep them in those kennels, because they don't want to pay to care for them properly. And, the reason they tell you this, is so they seem like they care about the pups, but really they don't. We stayed here for a bachelorette party during Labor Day weekend. We were 9 people in total, and wanted to be able to stay pretty much in a large suite , so we decided to reserve a penthouse. We booked this penthouse because it was the biggest and had the most beds, but also because it was one of the few that had an outdoor seating area (very important in this climate!). The penthouse is located on the top floor of the hotel, which has a private elevator, so we were not bothered by anyone else during our stay at all. The rooms are pretty much exactly as pictured, and they were very clean when we arrived. There were plenty of towels and linens, and the kitchen was well-stocked with dishes, glasses, pots and pans, silverware, etc. Basically, everything you would need to cook a meal for yourselfyour group. The only thing I would say about the actual rooms is that there is no air conditioning. So, if you're traveling in the summer time and like to sleep cool at night, you should be aware of that. Even though it's located in the financial district, there are some apartments located next door to this hotel, and they are all rented out to college students who seem to enjoy staying up all night long. So, again, if you want to get a good night's sleep and don't mind things getting a little warm at night, then I would recommend staying here. If not, then you might want to find something else. The staff at this hotel was really amazing. Everyone was super friendly and helpful. They even let us check in early, which was awesome because we had been traveling all morning and just wanted to relax in our room. Also, since we were traveling from out of state, many of us did not have cars with us, so we had to walk everywhere. The location of this hotel is great because it's within walking distance of a lot of restaurants, bars, and stores, but it's not in the middle of all the crazy foot traffic. Basically, you can walk anywhere you'd want to go, and you don't have to worry about being right in the middle of everything. So overall, I would definitely recommend staying at this hotel if you're looking for a place to stay in Boston. It's a little bit more expensive than other places in the area, but I think it's worth it.

This is another place I always meant to try when I lived in Madison but never did. I had a gift certificate from restaurants.com and decided to use it with my friend. I was really excited because I'd heard good things about it. The first thing we noticed when we walked in was how small the restaurant is. There are no tables, only bar-height chairs along the bar and a few high top tables. It's pretty dark inside too. We ordered drinks and some appetizers. What we didn't realize until after we ordered was that if you order an appetizer it comes with bread, which we didn't need. The bread wasn't anything special, just some thick sliced sourdough. For appetizers we had the bbq chicken flatbread and the wild mushroom bruschetta. The flatbread was covered in chicken, onion, cheddar cheese, and BBQ sauce. It was pretty good but not amazing. It would have been better if they hadn't put so much cheese on it. The bruschetta was very good. It came with four pieces of toast topped with mushrooms and mozzarella cheese. It was served with a little salad and some balsamic dressing. For our entrees we both ordered steak salad. The steak was really tender and well cooked, but there wasn't very much of it. The salad was very good though. It came with avocado, cucumber, tomato, and blue cheese crumbles. I wish they had given us more steak, but the salad was very tasty. Overall I thought this place was okay. I think it would be a great place to go for happy hour, or to meet up with a group of people. It might be a little hard to carry on a conversation if you were only meeting with one person because it's so noisy. I probably wouldn't go back unless someone asked me to. I think it's just kind of overpriced for what it is, especially because we had to pay extra for the salad.

Never ordering from here again. - Carlos G., Yelp Screenshot via Yelp It's hard to know where to begin with this one. A few months ago, there were nearly 500 reviews of the restaurant on Yelp, and only six of them gave the joint five stars. The rest were either one star (68) or two star (320). Since then, things haven't gotten any better for Mr. Delivery - that number has actually dropped slightly, to around 450 reviews, with over 70 one stars and 250 two stars. Now, when you look at the reviews, this is what you see: Screenshot via Yelp Yelp seems to have deleted all the reviews of Mr. Delivery that came before June 22nd. Why? Well, according to Yelp, "Yelp takes action on behalf of businesses who have allegedly paid someone to write fake reviews about them on Yelp. We have strong evidence that Mr. Delivery violated our terms of service by doing this, which is also misleading to consumers." Whoa, wait a minute. This is a serious accusation. Are we really supposed to believe that a business would pay people to write fake positive reviews about its services? That's...crazy. However, Yelp isn't the first one to accuse Mr. Delivery of faking positive reviews. As a matter of fact, that very same allegation appeared in a 2012 news report from the local ABC affiliate in New York City. In the piece, reporter Keldy Ortiz cited an anonymous source who worked at a PR firm that was hired by some of the city's restaurants to create positive reviews. The source named several restaurants, including Mr. Delivery, as clients, and claimed that employees of the PR firm wrote positive reviews for these businesses. "We offer customers 100 money back guarantee if we can't deliver 5-star rating review," the source told Ortiz. Mr. Delivery has denied the accusations in both the 2012 news report and Yelp's recent announcement. In response to Yelp's announcement, the company released the following statement: We believe Yelp's decision is unfair and unjustified. Mr. Delivery takes pride in providing great customer service, and we have never engaged in the practice of paying for favorable reviews. We're disappointed by Yelp's decision and struggling to understand the rationale behind their actions. Over the past few weeks, we have been in touch with Yelp regarding the removal of Mr. Delivery as a business listing on Yelp's site. To date, Yelp has provided no specific explanation for why Mr. Delivery is being removed from the site. Instead, Yelp has stated that "Yelp takes action on behalf of businesses who have allegedly paid someone to write fake reviews about them on Yelp." This statement is false. Mr. Delivery has never paid anyone to write fake reviews nor do we believe that we did anything that could warrant the removal of our business listing. While we continue to work with Yelp to reinstate our business listing, we encourage our customers to continue to provide us with honest feedback on our Yelp page. This is perhaps the part where we say something like, "So, how do you explain all those one and two star reviews, Mr. Delivery?" But we won't do that because we don't want to get sued for libel. Besides, despite the fact that Yelp seems to think Mr. Delivery is guilty of faking positive reviews, the jury will probably remain out on this one until proof emerges. Until then, let's just enjoy some of the funnier complaints from the restaurant's Yelp page:

Last Saturday, we waited about an hour and a half to get into Bacchanal. It's a bit pricy for a buffet but the food is pretty good. When we got in, we were greeted by a host who asked if we had reservations. We didn't, but he said that it was fine and led us to our table. The first thing you'll notice is that Bacchanal is huge. There's a main dining room with a bar and then a bunch of smaller dining rooms off to the side. The decor is pretty nice and there's a lot of natural light. The buffet itself is divided into stations. There's a carving station, a seafood station, a pasta station, a salad station, a dessert station, and more. The food is all fresh and there's a lot of variety. We started with the salad station. There was a nice selection of greens and toppings. We also tried the pasta station. The pasta was cooked perfectly and the sauce was very flavorful. For our main course, we went to the carving station. They had a roast beef that was cooked to perfection. We also tried the seafood station. The shrimp was fresh and the crab legs were delicious. Overall, we thought Bacchanal was a great experience. The food was fresh and there was a lot of variety. The price is a bit high, but it's worth it for the quality of the food.

Celebrity Chef Michael Mina brings his French cuisine to Las Vegas at his namesake restaurant, Michael Mina. Located in the Bellagio Hotel, the restaurant is known for its contemporary French cuisine with Mediterranean influences. The menu features seafood dishes like chilled lobster with avocado mousse, and a signature chicken pot pie. The menu is a la carte and guests may choose a three-course prix fixe menu for 65 per person. The restaurant also has a full bar. The restaurant's dining room seats 240 guests. It features a fireplace and a view of the Bellagio fountains. There is a private dining room available for groups and a patio for al fresco dining. Opened in 1998, Michael Mina is one of the original restaurants at the Bellagio and is still a favorite among Las Vegas diners. The other ghost is of the Emperor Norton, who was a prominent businessman. He's also known as the "Eccentric of San Francisco." He had a heart attack while dining at the hotel, and collapsed on the stairway leading to the main dining room. People have reported seeing him wandering around the hotel. Aside from the ghosts, I've always wanted to visit San Francisco, and staying at The Palace Hotel would be the icing on the cake. I would love to stay in one of the Victorian-style rooms. I guess I am not in the Trailhead club. Walking into a new place can sometimes be a bit awkward. Where to go, where to stand, seat yourself or not, what do you order - this stuff makes us humans feel uncomfortable and basically just an outsider. But when it comes down to our beloved hiking trails that we have been visiting for years now - on foot - things are much easier. They belong to us thanks to all of those who have hiked before us. Trails tend to stick together. In Germany we don't call these "trails": for me they are simply paths! The word "Trail" is so often used today, but that doesn't mean that there aren't any in other places around the world. Some people say that there shouldn't even be trails at all because then everybody will start building them which would lead to damage (or destruction). Of course if someone wants to build a trail, heshe should ask permission from all relevant parties. That means landowners as well as people living close by like farmers etc.. We try to respect each others boundaries and generally want everyone enjoy their land (even though some might think differently!). The locals also appreciate "trails" being developed. Local hikers will only use these paths once or twice a year and most times only during summer months. So having a walking path available to use 365 days per year takes care off one major problem. Most Germans spend their time in their car's... that does dmg to the environment. Having a nicely maintained trail gives people something interesting to do while driving around. It brings jobs, money and pride to local governments and businesses alike.

Seafood lovers would do well to try Hillel's. It has been around quite awhile but just opened up it's doors on West 47th Street 8th Avenue last year. This isn't something new for NYC as there are several restaurants serving good quality sea food throughout Manhattan. But what makes this one special? Well for starters it offers some of the best scallop dishes in town. Let me tell ya they make 'em fresh right here in house everyday. They come cooked perfectly in a light dipping sauce and topped with crisp green onions served alongside their signature hand cut fries. Their fish cakes are also very popular. They feature 2 different types of fish; cod and haddock. You can choose between having them fried, baked, grilled, or seared. Fresh fish straight from the water tastes much better than any frozen fillet and these sure taste fresher. That said, Hillels isn't cheap by any means. So if you aren't ready to spend too much money then Shinjuku Fish Market might be your best bet. If you want upscale and gourmet fare then you should head over to Hillels. Make sure you don't skip dessert though because they serve up some pretty tasty desserts including creme brulee.

If you like grease and slow service, you'll like this place. Was really hoping for something different when we arrived but it's typical bar type food you can get anywhere. My steak was overcooked, fish was undercooked and the sides were a bit dry. I had no idea what to expect from Greenhouse Grill Wine Bar so I didn't research menu items too much beforehand. As I walked into the restaurant I felt immediately relaxed by the atmosphere - there are lots of windows that look out onto the lush green trees in front of the restaurant offering plenty of natural light, plants and beautiful flowers throughout the dining room...and my absolute favorite...a HUGE terrace with two outdoor fireplaces overlooking St Johns Town Center! The staff is professional yet very friendly. We ordered several appetizers which came out quickly and our meal started fairly promptly after as well (expect for the 2nd course). Our waiter recommended an entree from their wine list and order 1 sounded good. After eating one bite (which wasn't bad) I noticed large chunks of rock hard meat still attached to meat on both fish fillets I received. They immediately brought me another plate and I asked if they could bring us a couple more plates since we weren't finished eating yet due to how much meat we had left uneaten on each dish...we ended up having 3 bites total upon finishing the second courses. Not sure what the deal was because everything else was fine and it didn't seem like the problem was with the cooking. It may have been not heatingcooking something properly? Either way, would definitely avoid unless they change something about their menu or prepare the food differently.

Much hype for the chocolate man. Although I'm not a big chocolate person, I figured.... I was in Vegas! I'll give it a shot. The Milk Chocolate had, as expected, the most flavor. If you like this type of thing, go ahead and get some. The other two were more subtle... but really good nonetheless. Think about how great chocolate is paired with another vanilla-like dessert such as a cheesecake or tiramisu now imagine that same flavor profile with four different kinds of cacao. One word of caution: I tried Coke and Pepsi Max in combination; both are delicious, so do what you will with that knowledge.

First of all, you have to go to this restaurant for the entertainment factor. Nobody goes to Disneyland for the great hot dogs right? You go to this restaurant for the characters and not only that but because it is located on Main Street USA (Disneyland's main street). I think even if Disney didn't add attractions or rides to an area they would still be able to maintain interest by adding a new character or two to the restaurants each year. With that being said, it was already announced that Pixar Place will be getting some awesome additions in 2013 so keep your eyes open! Secondly, my family went there last night with our 4-year old niece who had never been before. She loved it! We were worried that she might get bored after waiting around awkwardly for something like 30 minutes but we had no issues whatsoever. This is one of those places where you can just relax and really enjoy spending time together as a whole unit without having to worry about her running off like many other small kids do at Disneyland. When we first walked through the doors she screamed so loud when she saw Nemo that it actually startled me. It is a very special place for young children because almost every character has their own little play area set up where children are free to run around and interact with them however they choose. In addition, since most of these smaller guests cannot yet ride any of the attraction vehicles on their own, parents can always accompany them while they watch the show from the comfort and safety of their own cars. Our family went over to Buzz Lightyear's Space Ranger Spin and watched Toy Story 3 from inside our car. Need more convincing?! Check out what Mykaela had to say: This place is amazing!! Like seriously, I've literally never seen anything quite like it. The more you look into it the more amazed you become. Plus you meet SO MANY CUTE CHARACTERS. You know how when you see pictures online everyone looks cute and amazing and perfect but then you're standing next to them and realize "oh yeah...they're just people too." Well, none of that applies here. These characters ARE amazing and perfect!!! They come bearing gifts of stuffed animals and candy and stickers and THEN THEY PULL OUT STUFFING FOR YOU AND GIVE IT TO YOU ITS LIKE A CHILDHOOD DREAM COME TRUE!!!!!!!!!!!!! I knew going in that I wanted to write a long post about this specific restaurant because it truly blew us away. There isn't much else I could possibly say to convince others to give it a shot. I'm used to the cringe-worthy bar tabs that can be accrued while bar hopping in Tempe. After frequenting Baseline Pub on several occasions with my friends, I've been pleasantly suprised by their drink specials this summer and wanted to share them here for once reader of mine who may not have known about them yet! First up is 1 Wednesday. From 5 p.m.-7 p.m. Wednesdays an all drinks are just a dollar each. The deal does include beer, wine and even cocktails (of course). It's always a good time spent at Baseline. This one was especially great during the month of July because it coincided perfectly with some awesome storms we had rolling through AZ. Another special they run on Thursdays from 5p.m.-8p.m. is their Brews Bites event which includes five beers and ten appetizers such as corn dogs, nachos and chips. Throw in your best lady friend or your significant other and you're set for happy hour. They also do a similar thing called Happy Hour Saturdays where they offer discounted appetizer deals but no alcohol served. Either way, you'll definitely walk out of there feeling like you got away with something... Actually, it will probably come back to bite me in the ass when I need money again next week.

Some of the reviews seem dated and it appears the show may have changed up a little since changing venues over the past few years. I just stopped in this week, for their annual Hairspray Night (check out my review from last year), to see what all they've added to their menu. It was pretty good! The first thing you notice when walking through the door is that the new location has been completely renovated into an industrial styled restaurant with lots of exposed brick, wood paneling, and metal accents. From there, you walk though an open kitchen onto another "lounge area" where patrons could watch as food came out of the kitchens across the way. This part still had some pool tables, but then we moved upstairs to the main dining room. There are plenty of windows here which makes this place feel bright and airy during most hours of operation, even if you aren't eating outside on one of their beautiful outdoor patios. The seating capacity is limited, so make reservations far in advance. We made ours about 6 weeks ahead of time for two people. By the way, their website does not list any specials or events at the moment. I started off by ordering the jambalaya pasta. It was loaded down with shrimp, crawfish, beans, onions, mushrooms, celery, garlic, artichokes, bread crumbs, sausage, Parmesan cheese, and ranch dressing. Not bad at all; however, the flavor profile didn't really do anything special for me compared to other versions I've tried. I would recommend that your order be prepared exactly how the chef instructs it - no more, no less. And don't get me wrong, it tasted good...just nothing unique. On top of everything else, the sauce wasn't very thick and needed thickerening. My girlfriend had the fried catfish po-boy, which comes served with coleslaw and honey mustard dipping sauce. She loved this dish, saying that she thought it had great flavors. I agree with her assessment also, although like the above mentioned dish, some might find its uniqueness lacking. Again, it did taste good, and the portion size was large enough for both of us. If you want something a bit lighter on the stomach, there's a full bar serving all kinds of drinks including beer, wine, cocktails, milkshakes, and specialty drinks such as Dirty Martini or Mai Tai. They also carry individually packaged appetizers as well as soups and salads. Overall, the food was decent, but nothing spectacular. If you don't mind sitting indoors overlooking their big parking lotgarage, their prices aren't too crazy. You can definitely eat reasonably priced meals here without having to spend a fortune. But if you just wanted to enjoy a nice evening out somewhere different than the same old chain restaurants, go check them out!

This is the old Rigatony's on Brown Rd- If you've never been, it has a Buca di Bepo-ish, before Buca was cool, sort of feel. They even serve their house wine in a coffee cup! They had been there since 1954, but the owner decided to retire. Citing issues with the landlord, the owner put a sign on the door stating that they were closed for renovations. They had previously told the landlord they were going to retire. They did a quick "renovation" that consisted of screwing a piece of plywood over the windows with the word "closed" on it. If you walk up to the building, there is nothing out of the ordinary, it just looks closed. The building is owned by the City of Canton. The city acquired it when they expanded the road. The city then sold the building to the current landlord. The landlord is a private citizen. He also owns the parking lot the restaurant is on. He has a lease with the city to rent the parking lot. The restaurant owner is now suing the landlord. He alleges that the landlord is keeping him from doing business and is interfering with his lease with the city. I find it interesting that the restaurant owner's lease with the city is worth more than his lease with the landlord, but he chose not to renew the lease with the landlord.

First of all, you have to go to this restaurant for the entertainment factor. Nobody goes to Disneyland for the great hot dogs right? You go to this restaurant for the environment and the entertainment. A skilled orchestra, of French speaking wait staff, playing out tunes of the Beatles, and many other American hits, while the waiters sing and dance around the room. They take reservations and seating is typically for 2 hours. They seat you and bring the menus, wine list, and an appetizer plate of olives and bread. After you order, they bring the main course and then dessert and coffee. The food is excellent, but the show is what you come for. The food is served in the traditional French way. The entertainment is not a show. It's a way of life. They are not actors in a show. They are waiters, bartenders, and cooks. They are very talented and they work their way through the room singing and dancing and they all sing the Beatles song Yellow Submarine and they have fun doing it. The men have on black tuxedos and the women on white dresses. The restaurant has been around since the late 60's and they have been doing this show for a long time. They have had a lot of fun with it, and they bring a lot of fun to the guests. I have seen some very upscale restaurants that try to do something like this. If you have ever been to the French restaurant at Disneyworld in Florida, or the Napa Rose restaurant at Disneyland, you will know what I mean. They don't have the same level of talent, and they don't have the same level of fun. This restaurant is actually in an old train station in the old part of town, right across from the Eiffel Tower. The building itself is worth the price of admission. This is a good restaurant for the whole family, and it is a great place to take a date. It's a good place to celebrate a special occasion, or just to have a nice night out. You don't need to dress up, but some people do. It's a little more casual than most places like it. The price of a meal for 2 will run you about 120 to 150 for a full meal with a bottle of wine and dessert. That might sound expensive, but if you compare it to a meal at the French restaurant at Disneyworld in Florida, or the Napa Rose at Disneyland, then it's a pretty good deal. I've been there twice, and I have had a good time both times. The food was excellent, and the entertainment was great. You can check out their website at ChezLouisPhantom.com. You can book a reservation online, but be aware that the site is in French, and it might be easier to call them or email them. As with any restaurant in a tourist area, it can be a little bit difficult to get a reservation. If you know you are going to be in the area, it's better to call ahead. Even if you are just passing through Paris, you should try and stop by the Chez Louis Phantom for a drink or a meal, or just to say that you were there. It's just something that everyone should do. This restaurant is just a short walk across the river from the Eiffel Tower.

What a great introduction to the Cirque de Soleil chain. I have never been to one of their shows and after seeing this water stage show, I would love to see a full Cirque de Soleil production. The cast of 21 performers came from all over the world. I counted 8 different countries of origin. The performers were energetic, talented, engaging, and daring. The show was fast paced and non-stop action. I loved the set and staging. It was an interesting twist on the traditional circus tent. I would give the show an A. Although the set is very interesting, the action itself is not. It is at times thrilling and I would have loved to see some real stunts instead of just a bunch of acrobatics. It is not the traditional circus we all have grown up with. It was more entertainment than a true circus show. I wanted to be wowed and I was not. I am sure that there is more to this show than I saw. We were not able to sit in the first few rows, so maybe the effect is not as great in those seats. It was interesting to see the different nationalities represented in the cast. It was also interesting to see the many different levels of ability represented. There were some amazing performers and some that just looked like they were making it up as they went along. The music and the singing were wonderful. I just loved the singing. I would recommend this show to anyone that enjoys acrobatics and fast paced action. It is not a show that everyone would appreciate. I think that we saw a version that was still in rehearsal, so it may have been more polished by the time we saw the show in Dallas. BEING SORT OF A NARCISSIST, I STARTED WRITING A MEMOIR... CHAPTER 3: WHAT I LEARNED IN JUNIOR HIGH Inspired after reading about Pablo Picasso's legendary ways with women, I drew a moustache on my face and then plunged into my junior high years. I'm not sure where I was going with this or why I thought it would be interesting, but I started working on this book. The title is "A Thousand Farewells: A Memoir of a Jewish Boy in a Catholic School," although it's never really been about that. Just trying to tell some stories about my life and make it kind of funny. And now, while I'm not even sure where this book is going, I'm going to start posting some of it on this blog. The stories might be a little long, but if you're interested, you can click the "read more" link to get the whole thing. CHAPTER 3: WHAT I LEARNED IN JUNIOR HIGH I learned that you can be popular if you have a moustache. Inspired after reading about Pablo Picasso's legendary ways with women, I drew a moustache on my face and then plunged into my junior high years. My dad was a shoe salesman, and he would say to us, "You're lucky, because I'm home every night, and I'm making good money." My mom worked at a post office, and she was home every night, too. So I guess we were lucky. My parents didn't know it at the time, but they were about to have two more children. And if you're keeping score at home, that would be three kids. We also had a dog. I lived in the suburbs, which was nice, and I went to public school. I was a quiet, shy kid, but I had a lot of friends. I'll call the people I hung out with the popular kids. They were the ones who had the coolest stuff. They were the ones who got invited to the best parties. They were the ones who everyone wanted to be like. Everyone wanted to be like them, but I wasn't one of them. I was a kid who wasn't in their social stratosphere, and I didn't have a cool car, or a big-screen TV, or a stereo. And I didn't have any cash. But I did have a moustache. I started drawing one on my face, and then I got this idea. What if I just shave it off and don't do anything with it? Then maybe it will grow back. And when it did, I'd be like, Hey, I have a moustache, and everyone would think I was cool. So I did. I shaved off my moustache, and I waited. A few weeks went by, and my moustache didn't come back. I was so upset. I had wasted a lot of time waiting for that thing to come back. My mom kept asking me, "Do you want your moustache back?" "I'm just waiting for it to grow back," I'd tell her. And then one day, I was sitting in the front seat of our 1958 Plymouth Savoy, with my parents in the back, and I saw something. I saw a tiny little strand of hair coming out of my lip. I thought, That's my moustache. I leaned over and I picked it up. It was a baby moustache. I knew it was going to be a great moustache. I started to shave it off. And that was the beginning of my junior high years. I started at a new school. I was in the seventh grade, and the eighth grade was a whole different building. I started walking down the hall and I heard a voice behind me. It was a voice I'd heard before. It was the voice of a girl I'd been friends with in the old neighborhood. I turned around and it was a girl I'd been friends with in the old neighborhood. I said, "Hey, how are you?" She said, "Hi." And then she said, "Hey, you look cool." "Cool?" I said. "I just shaved off my moustache," I told her. "Do you like it?" "I think it's cool," she said.

This place is located in Aria across from Marquee. I was told this was one of the top burger spots on the strip and they weren't lying. I would not recommend their burgers over any other fast food places but there are some things that do stand out about The Cheeseburger Stand. I had had a taste of The Burger Stand before, unfortunately when we walked into the restaurant we saw two older gentlemen talking to eachother inside the door! So it took me a second or so to realize what's happening..you can get a hold of them by calling them up for your order. When you walk through the front doors you will see a bartop where people wait while their drinks are made ready...that usually takes 3-5 minutes. Once all their drinks are prepared you enter another room filled with tables and chairs outside. You're sitting at a wooden table surrounded by other customers who seem like they aren't happy to be here...it's really kindof depressing seeing how unhappy these people look. They have an employee standing next to you who tries his best to cheer them up which annoys some if the patrons because he doesn't know them well enough yet. As soon as you sit down you hear the music coming off a tv set and you immediately get that "cheese" feeling again...that's right I said cheesy!! There are also several cool looking menu boards with different food items available such as breakfast burritos (which were actually pretty good) and hot dogs covered with cheese curls which looks like a giant grilled cheesen sandwich with a bunch of toppings on it...I didn't try those though. For dessert I had ordered the cheese fries which consist of french fries topped with melted cheddar cheese and then fried until crisp again; It was yummy!!! The menu price range from 4 - 8 and I'd personally go ahead and use the 3 coupon towards their hamburgers since the prices (6-10) seem high compared to the other restaurants around town. If you ask nicely they'll also give you free refills later on in the evening with no limit!!!! Even though they only serve beer and wine there is still plenty of room left for liquor too. When you come inside you find yourself paying more attention to the employees serving the food than to the food itself...they always seemed pleasant and helpful so don't worry about getting lost in their tables! One thing I am disappointed about really is that The Burger Stand isn't open everyday...there should really be more hours and days. Also I wish there was a vegetarian option instead of meat. All kidding aside though, The Burger Stand has become my favorite spot on the Strip and definitely a must stop while staying in Las Vegas!

Our waitress was able to pull up our waiter's name so I could quickly find his phone number when talking to her about my bill (she asked me how much money I wanted before she returned to help us). She reeled off several different options with each one being significantly more expensive than what I ordered, but knowing that the quality of their service made it worth it. Onions, peppers, cheddar cheese, lettuce, tomatoes and mayonnaise make this a great meal even if you only want a small bite. The sausage and stuffed beehives salad also comes loaded with veggies - corn, baby carrots, green beans, onions and jalapenos. There are an abundance of homemade pickles available as well as large piles of tartar sauce, ranch dressing, mayo, relish, tomato paste and swede jam wrapped around the side of the plate. My salad had the most delicious pickled red bell pepper with onion and jalapeno slices - there wasn't anything in it that didn't taste good. However the other ingredients left something to be desired. In fact,the tomato cheese dip on the bottom half of the plate tasted flat and uninteresting. I liked the peach snifter tea though - it contained the same ingredients as the savory dishes above, but with just a hint of spice and sweetness. A lot of people have complained about the high price of these meals, however its hard to argue against the value since they are of such a high quality once you get past the price tag. If you ever live down by Chapel Hill or Winston-Salem, stop into FBC if you are hungry and looking for some southern comfort food! I highly recommend the peaches.

I guess I am not in the Trailhead club. Walking into a new place can sometimes be a bit awkward. Where to go, where to stand, seat yourself or not, what size hand do you hold your coffee mug with and so on...and now this space has an official name!! The Trailhead Cafe is located on the first floor of the Welcome Centre near the north entrance (from around 11am - 4pm). Marked with banners, maps, welcome signs, baskets of food, chairs and table covers, the cafe has everything that would help you get settled and feel at home here. Recently I was invited by The Trailhead cafe's founders, Andy Edie Dufresne, to tour their space. Their vision for the next few years is clear: "We are aiming to become one of Winnipeg's favourite places across all sectors including business, sports, community groups, music, and festivals as well as weddings! We want it to be inviting, fun and welcoming for anyone who wants to come experience something different and wonderful. Our goal is to make 'thinking outside of the box' enjoyable while still maintaining a friendly atmosphere for everyone." Andy worked for many years as a general managerowner of restaurants in the city before taking ownership of his own restaurant which has since expanded into two locations. Edie grew up with a very active family of 5 children and always knew she wanted to have her own space to create memories for them too. She started organizing shows and events when they were teenagers and fell in love with the concept and venue management world right away. Since then, the couple started managing Weddings By Edie, a wedding planning company that specialises in creating memorable and beautiful daypart experiences through unique venues like the Prairie Trail Inn. While the cafe sells breakfast items on weekdays, lunch is served on weekends. While the space will continue to host local musicians throughout the year, the cafe plans to focus more heavily on catering events for parties and corporate meetings this fall. Working together with their event planner Megan Nicholack Riehl, the cafe aims to offer a variety of menu options from breakfast sandwiches and salads to full meal service, featuring bread, pastries, hot dishes, desserts and smoothies. In addition to snacks and drinks, they plan to feature fresh juices and coffees, and even have a rotating selection of bread-based cookies, chips and crackers available during certain times. As with any small business, getting customers into doors means maximizing sales and marketing opportunities within these settings. Additionally, the team hopes to expand its hours later this winter once the cafe gets back to business after winter break ends. Their timeline may appear ambitious but they both agree they know how important it is to keep people coming back despite tough economic times. They also believe having a live music venue nearby can play a significant role in helping them reach their goals. With an outdoor seating area and extensive parking lots, the cafe thinks they might see a large increase in visitors over the summer months especially if there are musical performances scheduled alongside other festival activities. To learn more about the cafe, check out the website or follow TravelandWynnex on Instagram

I've been wanting to check this place out ever since I read my fellow Yelper and friend Dyanna's review! So when we decided to have one of our lunch dates , we headed there for a quick look. We both were excited about the fact that it was not too far from work (and as if by coincidence, right after her review you guys posted!), so off we went to find someplace to sit down for a bite. The atmosphere inside is very casual, which definitely helps me relax while I eat! There isn't a whole lot going on in terms of decor - just basic chairs, tables, and light bulbs hanging over head. The waitstaff are friendly but seem to be more concerned with getting the food to us quickly than actually listening to what I'm saying and answering questions. Our food arrived pretty much at the same time: 3 small plates served family-style, along with 2 orders of cheese curds and fries. For 5 each, these came up to the full price of 10 - not the worst deal considering how fast they ate away! It took a bit longer than usual to get everything cooked because of all the people. At least 7 or 8 people had already come through the door before we got ours when we ordered, so we didn't know exactly how long it would take them to prepare everything. Still, tables ended up being cleaned at different times during our visit to help keep it busy enough around peak hours without overwhelming everyone else trying to enjoy their meals. The first course was sausage peppers (8). These were nice sausages nicely seasoned with some mayo mustard. All three sides were included in our total, although we did receive a free side for ordering foods that normally go for 33 (appetizer platter). While I usually don't do vegetarian options for myself, I really enjoyed eating these and felt like I could do this every day for lunch now! Next was green beans (4), which were greener than expected - maybe because they weren't cooked until later? They were still good though; tender and moist. A little sweet, and nothing overly spicy, they paired well with the meat dishes. Then we moved onto chicken corn chowder (6) which seemed to be quite popular. Again, once again, these were tasty and served piping hot. Made with stock and cream instead of milk, it's a decent way to fill up your bowl without spending too much money. After that, we tried some breaded fish (9), which I thought was pretty good. It came with chips, salad, and sauce with it. My favorites were the chipotle ranch and ginger ale with chili. Both of those flavors were very good, especially with the dip and the chips. The fish itself wasn't bad either, although its texture actually reminded me of something between mackerel salmon. Not sure why that is...but whatever it was, it was fine to eat. I think it probably wouldn't be great for "the 12 hour kind of hungry," but otherwise, I liked the flavor. We also tried some beef patties (13), which were better than advertised. Even though they looked like ground hamburger, they tasted a lot like real steak with a touch of saltiness to give the meat some kick! The sauce was delicious, even if it caused a slight dryness on the outside of the pattie. The fries had a strong garlic taste to them and were perfect. If anything, it was an average meal for the cost - definitely not terrible, but nothing spectacular either. Overall, the only thing I can complain about is that no matter where I tried to go, they kept closing the kitchen as soon as dinner service started. This meant I missed out on another few bites of food, which might have turned into some other things I wanted to try, but never would have in such limited time. Overall, we're glad we chose Bistro Do Canto over Cafe Bocuse to meet up with Dyanna on our date night! And the prices aren't too bad compared to most restaurants in the area. Not expensive enough to warrant sitting here for extended periods of time, but cheap enough to make it worth coming back for multiple entrees per person. Definitely recommend checking out their website to see exactly the menu they offer, as there are certain items they'll always offer at this location, others will change based on demand.

I'm used to the cringe-worthy bar tabs that can be accrued while bar hopping in Tempe. After frequenting Baseline Pub on several occasions with my friends, I've been pleasantly suprised by how well they manage to keep a relatively low price point for some of their drinks and offer unique pub food items within an upper tier location. But one thing has always been the same: The prices are incredibly high. For example, any time we would order a Bloody Mary, it was 12.50; for two people at lunchtime it could easily get you out the door around 20. My friend ordered a classic margarita (the "6" option) without extra chilies (5), which is not uncommon for Margaritas from this bar. And although we had no idea what we were getting into when we walked in, after our first drink I realized the shaker bottle really wasn't full of booze - it looked like just water - so we asked if they'd refill it for us. We got told yes, but it didn't take long before the bartender came back over saying the shaker was empty again - and blaming himherself for not knowing how much liquor was actually in there. Needless to say, we ended up paying more than 10 each for our entire short visit. In comparison, other bars have similar prices for less punchy drink options, or even cheaper ones. One nice perk about Baseline Pub is its menu. Servers usually hit several staples off your basic burger menu, including couple different appetizers such as bacon cheese fries, chicken nuggets and macaroni cheese bowls. Then all you need to do is add toppings of your choice and enjoy your meal! Though I don't think this place will appeal to everyone's taste buds due to how expensive everything costs, it definitely makes a good base item to round out most meals or snacks. Baseline Pub has three locations across Arizona. Two are located in Mesa and Gilbert, and the third is in Scottsdale next to Good Luck Nick's Sports Bar. If you're looking to hangout while enjoying cheap drinks, then these places might be worth checking out.

CHAPTER 3: WHAT I LEARNED IN JUNIOR HIGH Inspired after reading about Pablo Picasso's legendary ways with women, I drew inspiration from this artist and decided to write a memoir. I was in Junior High when we had the Spanish Civil War (the Spanish presence won), so of course most of my classmates were obsessed with the era which ended up being the catalyst for many wars throughout history. One of my classmates moved away to live in New York City as she started her career there; since then, access to that memory has been difficult to obtain, but thanks to a wonderful daughter who recently graduated college, I have finally uncovered the source. It also turns out that while passing through Spain on one excursion, I happened upon the famous villa where Picasso stayed during his time there, Casa Milagros, now known as Villa Gesu. After arriving at the villa by bus that morning, I joined an admirer group behind the owner, Fernando Garcia de la Pena, who actually lived here, and the rest is history! In Chapter 1, I wrote about how Picasso acquired the title "Pablo" by marrying his first cousin, and in Chapter 2, I described what exactly fell into place before Picasso became an international superstar. However, I neglected something important regarding the events leading to me coming to love the man who would become Pablo - my mother. She died in 1957 at the young age of forty - two, having experienced much heartache over losing my father several years earlier. In the past few months, it took me some time to realize just what kind of person my mom really was. As a matter of fact, I couldn't recall ever meeting her until I got older than fourteen, or even ten, as I grew up. My dad was always gone working, traveling, or playing golf, leaving her alone all day every single day. So when she told us story after story about our "father" growing up, I naturally assumed he must've been someone special, as she mentioned him often enough to make certain that everyone remembered his name. So once I realized why she loved Angelique so much, it began to dawn on me just how remarkable her life truly was. With her successful business, raising six children alone while keeping a loving marriage intact, and balancing family and work, it seems that everything seemed pretty easy for her. But for a lot of people, their lives are filled with hard work and sacrifices, rather than happiness and ease. After all, did you meet any woman who doesn't struggle with pain? My mother certainly didn't overlook anything. From being thrown off a bridge because she hated bridges, to having to walk miles across town in order to find food at the local supermarket, most of my childhood memories revolved around hardship. When I left home at sixteen for the very first time, picking up your parents' belongings from the airport was one of those hardships. That was also when, like most single mothers do, she had to fend for herself and figure things out on her own. It should come as no surprise that such challenges eventually led her to my finding love. Not only did my parents never think I'd get hitched, they thought I wouldn't want anyone else because of the struggles they suffered together. The last thing they wanted was another child and yet somehow they found themselves falling in love anyway. Even today, when I look back on the relationship, I can still remember the night my mom walked into our bedroom singing that my husband and I could be together forever. This place is located in Aria across from Marquee. I was told this was one of the top burger spots on the strip and they weren't lying. I would not be surprised if there were more than a dozen different burgers on their menu, but that's just my guess based off what we ordered, plus an order of fries for each person - three patties with cheese, bacon, lettuce onions tomato and mustard all on a toasted bun. The cheeseburger at The Burger Bar at Cosmopolitan Las Vegas (Photo: Provided by David Sibley) I'm not going to lie to you guys ... This thing looks amazing. But it comes packed full of meat goodness so pick your poison because you're either gonna love this or hate this. We started out with the signature double-cheeseburger (14), which came with two thick beef patties, melted American cheese, chopped onion and hot sauce served between two large buns. It didn't disappoint us, though I have to say it wasn't quite as juicy as our grilled cheese before it. And when we tried getting both of 'em on the same fry, it got a little messy. Not too big a deal since these things are drenched in grease anyway. If you want something plainer, grab the triple-cheese steakburger (13). Or let me tell ya about the rare burger special! You get half a pound of tenderloin placed inside a crispy sesame seed brioche bun, topped with melted cheddar cheese, crisp onions rings and sliced jalapenos. It sounds pretty crazy until you taste it. Even better? A special side salad made up of romaine hearts, tomatoes, cucumber, avocado slices and feta cheese. Heaven. My only criticism? They should serve this without the bacon; maybe make it extra crispy instead of breaded like most places do. When in doubt, go with less is more. Next time try ordering The Platinum Burger (27). That's right. Topped with a fried egg, mozzarella, tomatoes, basil, oregano, green olives and caramelized onions. Mmmmmmm deliciousness. For dessert, we opted for the Chocolate Cake Ice Cream Pie (4.99). Look past how gross looking it is and it might still surprise y'all. So chocolate cake mixed with vanilla ice cream sandwiched together into a layer pie crust with whipped coconut creme fraiche spread over the layers. Yummo. Ice cream pies at The Burger Bar at Cosmopolitan Las Vegas (Photo: Courtesy photo) OK now go forth and eat every burger. Trust me. Once you've tasted them, everything else will seem tasteless. By the time I left junior high, I had come a long way in terms of understanding how to use my charm and charisma to attract the opposite sex. It's important to have high expectations for Costco's. Only because like a good club, you pay a cover. You get in. And have your world rocked. Prepare to wait and hour or two. Bring a book. And a shaving kit, because by the time you get to the checkout register, you'll have a beard. Ok, I kid. Maybe not. But be prepared to wait. 2. For example, I have to drive all the way to St. George to get Extra Light Virgin Olive Oil. costcofail 3. BATHROOMS!! The bathrooms are not very clean. It's a club. Let me feel exclusive. The negatives are not necessarily dealbreakers for my Costco membership. There is some real value in being a card carrying member. It's just this particular location that doesn't live up to my expectations. I've seen some really great locations. My standards are high.
